_readme: This is DATA, not code, and the file format is the argument. docs/PLAN/07 § Core
Principles: 'Templates MUST NOT have their own application logic (no per-template
backend code). Visual differences between templates = differences in component sets
+ theme variables + layout config -- all data, not code.' A template that lived in a
.ts file would be a template that could import something, and the first one that did
would break the rule for every template after it.
Two consumers read this file and neither may drift from the other: the seed command
(src/infra/db/seed.mts) and a test that validates it against the P0-20 schema
(test/reference-template.spec.ts). The test is the reason a later schema change
cannot silently invalidate the one template the product ships with.
Section order is docs/UI-UX/14 § Section Order, exactly.
changelog: First reference template. Ten sections in the docs/UI-UX/14 default order.

_why: configurable: false. An invitation with no cover is not an invitation, and
docs/FRONTEND/04 step 2 renders a non-configurable section whatever the user
chose. The consequence at publish time is deliberate: the two nicknames are
required even if the user never opens the hero section in the editor.
Parents are optional fields, not required. docs/PLAN/08 § Entity: Person marks
father_name and mother_name optional, and a required parent name would block
publication for anyone whose parents have died or who does not wish to name them.
configurable: false, per the task card: 'an invitation without event details is
not an invitation'. The required fields use the wildcard, so EVERY event needs a
date, a start time, a venue and an address -- two events where one is half-filled
publishes a page with a blank card on it (BR-4.2).
end_time is optional: a reception that runs until the guests leave has no end.
max_items 20, not the package's 200. docs/PLAN/09 caps STORAGE at 200 photos;
this caps what one grid DISPLAYS. Twenty images is already a heavy page on the
3G connection docs/UI-UX/14 assumes, and the public page has a JS and bytes
budget that a gallery is the easiest way to spend.
Coordinates are OPTIONAL even though this is the map section. docs/PLAN/08 says
maps_url is 'auto-generated from lat/long if empty', so a user who pasted a
Google Maps link and never touched the picker still has a working button. The
address is what is required, because it is what a guest reads.
MapsStatic, not an interactive SDK: docs/PLAN/00 § Maps keeps the map SDK out of
the public page for JS budget and per-load cost, and links out instead.
Enabled by default false, and this is the one section where that is a judgement
rather than a mechanic. Asking for money is a choice a couple makes deliberately;
a gift section that appears unless you turn it off asks on their behalf.
No required_fields. RSVP entries are guest-submitted after publication, so a
template that required them would make publishing impossible by construction --
which is why the canonical registry has no rsvp.* path at all (P0-20).
Closing needs the nicknames again -- it is the thank-you, and it signs off. They
are already required by the hero, so this adds no new obstacle to publishing.
collectMissingRequiredFields reports a path once per section that needs it, so
the user sees which sections are blocked rather than one anonymous field.
